verdict: NOT CONVERGED — 2 blockers, 4 P1 coverage gaps, 5 P2s. The identifier layer of this paper is in unusually good shape: 46 distinct bibliographic identifiers resolve, every PMID/PMCID/DOI grouped inside a reference entry belongs to one paper, every publication-type characterisation matches the record, and 16 of the 18 verbatim quotations are present word-for-word in the source named (the other 2 are unreachable and the paper says so). What fails is the layer above it — the sentences in §1.2 that characterise what the CITED LITERATURE does and does not do. Two of those are refuted by the very sources the row cites, and both err in the direction that enlarges this paper's contribution, which is the defect class Appendix A11/A24/A30/A31 already names.
central_claim: The NR4A3 5' fusion partner is a candidate — not established — stratification variable: a crude, confounded prognostic magnitude (7/15 vs 6/58 disease-specific death) whose own larger cohort says it is size-confounded, plus a directionally consistent but statistically inconclusive antiangiogenic-response signal of 0 of 3–5 TAF15 patients; prevalence 18.2 % (12.9–25.0).

blockers.where: §1.2, the 'Four literatures that had never been combined' table, TKI-response row (line 117), and the paragraph closing that section (line 124)
blockers.quote: | **TKI response** | responders are EWSR1, non-responders include every TAF15 patient [1,3,4,5,6] | never states a denominator in the primary text; never pooled | … The result is a belief that is stronger in the field's prose than in the field's data, and it has never been possible to say by how much, because nobody had put the counts in one place.
blockers.why_wrong: TWO OF THE FIVE SOURCES THE ROW ITSELF CITES STATE EVERY PER-ARM DENOMINATOR THIS PAPER POOLS, IN THEIR BODY TEXT, AND ONE OF THEM STATES BOTH COHORTS' COUNTS IN A SINGLE PARAGRAPH. Reference [4] (Stacchiotti 2020) writes, in its section 4 body text: "a retrospective study describing six Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumor (RECIST) partial responses of 10 NR4A3-positive EMCs; interestingly all patients who responded showed the EWSR1 fusion gene whilst no activity was observed in the two TAF15-positive patients included in the series", "four of 22 evaluable patients had a RECIST partial response (all of them with EWSR1 fusion)" and "all three TAF15-positive tumors included in this pazopanib trial failed to respond to pazopanib". Reference [5] (Jacobs & Lapeire 2021) writes, in its section 3 body text: "Six Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) partial responses, two stable diseases and two progressive diseases were noted. Intriguingly, all patients with an objective response (OR) had EWSR1 as translocation partner for NR4A3 while the two cases with progressive disease harbored a TAF15-NR4A3 translocation" and "Four out of 22 evaluable patients achieved a RECIST partial response, and all four were positive for the typical EWSR1-NR4A3 translocation. Of the three patients with TAF15 as translocation partner, none showed a response." Those are exactly 0/2 and 0/3 against 6/8 and 4/19 — the primary and secondary strata of §3.1 — with both cohorts' counts in one place in [5]. The manuscript CONTRADICTS ITSELF on the same point: §4.4 says "The **per-arm denominators** for both the sunitinib series and the pazopanib trial were read from reviews". A reader is told the field never stated the denominators, by a paper whose own denominators were read out of the field's statements of them. The honest residual claim — that nobody POOLED them, computed an interval, or stated that the interval overlaps its comparator — survives untouched; the denominator clause and 'nobody had put the counts in one place' do not.

PubMed Central full text of Jacobs C, Lapeire L, Diagnostics (Basel) 2021;11(3):512, PMID 33799327, PMC7999686, doi 10.3390/diagnostics11030512, section 3 'NR4A3 Translocation in Extraskeletal Myxoid Chondrosarcoma (EMCS)'. blockers.quote: | **Partner prevalence** | TAF15 in roughly one EMC in five [7,8,9,10] | never pooled across series; the field quotes one cohort |
blockers.why_wrong: THIS IS THE ATTRIBUTION APPENDIX A30 RETRACTS, STILL LIVE AT A FIFTH SITE — ONE-OF-A-PAIR AGAIN, IN THE SAME DOCUMENT THAT NAMES THAT PATTERN FIVE TIMES (A5, A11, A16, A24, A31). A30 registers the retraction of "the ≈27 % the field routinely quotes" at "four sites in this document" — the Abstract, §3.5, the §5 claims bullet and A3 — on the ground that "No source for that quoting practice was held anywhere". 'The field quotes one cohort' is the same unsourced assertion about a quoting practice, in different words, and A30's 'where it was' column does not name §1.2, so the correction did not reach it. The record makes it worse rather than neutral: the only two sources in this paper's own reference list that state a general TAF15 share do NOT quote a single cohort's figure — reference [4] states "less frequently (about 20% of cases) to the transactivation domain of TAF15" and reference [12] states "less frequently (approximately 20%) to TAF15", and the third review in the citation set (reference [15], Remiszewski 2025) states no general share at all, writing only that variant partners "appear to shape phenotype rather than independently dictate outcome". So the document's live text still tells a reader that the field's prevalence figure comes from one referral cohort, while its own Appendix A30 says the field's figure is ≈20 % and sits inside the pooled interval. The two statements cannot both stand.

p1s.where: instrument coverage — the bracketed reference markers [1]–[15] throughout the manuscript; most load-bearing at §3.5 and the §5 claims bullet
p1s.quote: The two sources in the reference list that give a general TAF15 share — the disease review [4] and the introduction of the model-derivation paper [12] — both put it at about 20 %, which falls **inside** 12.9–25.0.
p1s.why_wrong: THE ATTRIBUTION IS CORRECT TODAY — I RESOLVED BOTH — AND NO INSTRUMENT READS IT. Exactly one committed test module opens this document (`research/manuscripts/tests/test_fusion_partner_prose_matches_its_artifact.py`; `grep -rln emc-fusion-partner-stratification --include=*.py` over the repository returns it, its two mutation harnesses, `claim_coverage.py` and `test_the_census_reads_every_publication_endpoint.py`). Its section-G identifier census matches `PMID`, `NCT` and `doi:` VALUES only (`_IDENT`); its `reference_entries` fixture reads `^\[\d+\] ` lines solely to GROUP identifiers inside an entry, and never binds the marker number `n` to a citation record. An in-text `[4]` or `[12]` is therefore not an identifier to any guard. Renumbering the reference list, inserting a reference, or retyping `[4]` as `[5]` would leave every test in the repository green while the paper credited the ≈20 % statement to a source that does not make it — which is the identical failure A11 registers for the metastasis PMCIDs and A30 for the ≈27 %. Two bindings do read the quotations themselves (`Appendix A30's verbatim quotation of reference [4]'s TAF15 share` and `… reference [12]'s`), but each binds only the digit `20` against `_ext_share(a)['percent_approx']`; the bracket number sits outside both regexes, so even swapping the two quotations' attributions passes.

p1s.where: instrument coverage — PMC identifiers; the load-bearing site is §3.3 / §5 / A11 / A24, where the metastasis attribution rests on 'PMC7563993 alone'
p1s.quote: the metastasis claim attributed to a single review (PMC7563993 alone — the only actual review among the four PMCIDs previously cited for it …) **is not established by either cohort, in either direction**
p1s.why_wrong: THE ONE ANCHOR FOR THIS PAPER'S MOST ATTRIBUTION-SENSITIVE CLAIM IS PRINTED IN THE ONE NOTATION NO CENSUS READS. The guard's own comment says it: 'A PMC id is printed 23 times in this manuscript and the artifact has no `pmc` field, so a PMC id is OUTSIDE this census and is read only by `lint_citations`' provenance test.' `lint_citations.py` asks only whether `PMC\d{6,9}` is anchored in some tracked JSON — not whether it is printed against the right paper. At §3.3, §5 and A24 the review is named as 'Stacchiotti 2020, PMC7563993' with NO DOI and NO PMID beside it (the DOI 10.3390/cancers12092703 appears only in reference entry [4] and in A30), so the section-G name-attachment test, which reads only PMID/NCT/DOI within 120 characters of a citation's short name, sees nothing there. Substituting any other anchored PMCID — PMC7999686, say, which is the other review in the reference list — would pass lint_citations (anchored), pass the ownership census (PMCIDs are not censused) and pass the name-attachment test (no readable identifier), leaving the paper's single-source metastasis attribution silently pointing at a different paper. The declaration documents the gap; it does not close it. For the record, the attribution is CORRECT at the pinned commit: PMC7563993 does carry the claim, in the sentence "A slightly better distant metastases-free survival was seen in patients carrying EWS-NR4A3 compared to TAF15-NR4A3 translocation."

p2s.where: §1.1, second paragraph of 'The disease, the drug class and the variable' (lines 101–103)
p2s.quote: *"Although often associated with prolonged survival, EMC have high rates of distant recurrences and disease-associated death"*, and *"Anthracycline-based chemotherapy, which is the first-line regimen used in STS, has low activity in this sarcoma subtype"* [12,4].
p2s.why_wrong: TWO VERBATIM QUOTATIONS, TWO REFERENCES, AND ONLY ONE OF THE TWO SOURCES CONTAINS EITHER. Both sentences are word-for-word in reference [12] (Bangerter, Introduction: 'Although often associated with prolonged survival, EMC have high rates of distant recurrences and disease-associated death.' and 'Anthracycline-based chemotherapy, which is the first-line regimen used in STS, has low activity in this sarcoma subtype'). Neither occurs in reference [4]: Stacchiotti 2020's full text says 'with an expected prolonged survival even though the risk of relapse is about 50%' and 'anthracycline-based, dacarbazine-based, and ifosfamide-based regimens', which is the same substance in different words. Citing a verbatim quotation to a source that does not contain it invites a reader to look for it there and not find it. The fix is `[12]` on the quotations, with [4] moved to whatever it is supporting.
p2s.evidence: PubMed Central full text of Bangerter JL et al., doi 10.1007/s13577-022-00818-x (PMC9813045), Introduction — both sentences present verbatim. PubMed Central full text of Stacchiotti S et al., doi 10.3390/cancers12092703 (PMC7563993) — neither sentence present. Attribution: PubMed/PMC.

p2s.quote: a 36.3-point gap, post-hoc Fisher p = 0.0034, and the first magnitude this contrast has ever had.
p2s.why_wrong: ONE-OF-A-PAIR: §3.3'S COPY SELF-CLARIFIES AND THE ABSTRACT'S DOES NOT. §3.3 writes '**This is the first magnitude the prognostic contrast has ever had** — before Huang's table was read, the "pool" was a single-cohort Wilson interval and this document said so', which makes plain that 'first magnitude' means first POOLED magnitude in THIS document. The Abstract prints the clause bare, where it reads as a claim about the literature — and the literature contradicts it. Agaram 2014's own abstract states 'only 1 of 16 patients with EWSR1-rearranged tumors died of disease, in contrast to 3 of 7 (43%) TAF15–rearranged tumors', a published per-partner disease-specific-death contrast of 36.7 points, eleven years earlier; §3.3 of this very manuscript prints those same integers two lines above the sentence. Same shape as A16, which the paper registers as a blocker: bounding one copy of a claim and leaving the other standing.
p2s.evidence: PubMed abstract and PMC full text of Agaram NP et al., Hum Pathol 2014;45(5):1084–91, PMID 24746215, PMC4015728, doi 10.1016/j.humpath.2014.01.007 — 'Follow-up showed that only 1 of 16 patients with EWSR1-rearranged tumors died of disease, in contrast to 3 of 7 (43%) TAF15–rearranged tumors.' Manuscript §3.3 at the pinned commit prints '3/7 = 42.9 % vs 1/16 = 6.2 % (Agaram)'. Attribution: PubMed/PMC.

p2s.where: §3.3, the metastasis paragraph; restated in §5 and Appendix A7
p2s.quote: the largest series to test metastasis by partner *directly* reports **P = .728** on its own three-way table
p2s.why_wrong: THE SUPERLATIVE IS CARRIED ENTIRELY BY AN UNDEFINED WORD. The series in question is Huang 2023 (n = 58). Paioli 2021 is larger (n = 67, 62 partner-assigned) and does test metastasis by partner: its abstract reports 'Patients carrying the NR4A3-EWS translocation had a trend in favor of better DFS (p = 0.08) and DMFS (p = 0.09) compared with the patients with NR4A3-TAF15', and this manuscript cites that DMFS p-value twice. 'Largest' is therefore true only under 'directly', meaning as a cross-tabulation rather than as time-to-event — a distinction no cited source draws, no artifact field records, and the sentence itself never defines. §2.3a bounds this superlative to the citation set, which is a different limitation and does not reach this one. Either define 'directly' where it is used, or state it as 'the larger of the two cohorts that publish counts'.
p2s.evidence: PubMed abstract of Paioli A et al., Ann Surg Oncol 2021;28(2):1142–1150, PMID 32572850, doi 10.1245/s10434-020-08737-7 (n = 67; 50 NR4A3-EWS, 10 NR4A3-TAF15, 1 TCF12, 1 TFG; DMFS p = 0.09 by translocation). PubMed abstract of Huang SC et al., Mod Pathol 2023;36(7):100161, PMID 36948401, doi 10.1016/j.modpat.2023.100161 (58 FISH-confirmed EMCs). Attribution: PubMed.

p2s.quote: The only partner-differential reported is a scoring-threshold one: the carfilzomib + venetoclax and carfilzomib + doxorubicin combinations scored **synergistic** in the EWSR1 model and **additive** in the TAF15 model
p2s.why_wrong: THE SOURCE REPORTS OTHER DIFFERENCES BETWEEN THE TWO MODELS, SO 'THE ONLY' IS TRUE ONLY OF DRUG RESPONSE AND THE SENTENCE DOES NOT SAY SO. Bangerter's Results report that the second model 'harbors two additional likely pathogenic mutations … beside a … alteration that has been classified as a VUS', and that the copy-number profiles differ between the two models (gains in chromosomes 1 and 8 in one; a chromosome 8 amplification with losses in chromosomes 2 and 6 in the other). Those are per-tumour genomic differences and not partner effects — which is exactly the reading §3.7 wants — but an unrestricted 'the only partner-differential reported' invites a reader to check the paper and find differences it does not mention. Scoping the sentence to drug response costs three words. The synergy/additivity reading itself is verbatim-correct: 'Drug synergy was found for [USZ20-EMC1] cell models using both combinations … and an additive effect in the [USZ22-EMC2] model.'
p2s.evidence: PubMed Central full text of Bangerter JL et al., doi 10.1007/s13577-022-00818-x (PMC9813045), 'Molecular characterization of USZ20-EMC1 and USZ22-EMC2' and 'Functional characterization …'. Attribution: PubMed/PMC.

identifier_result: 46 distinct bibliographic identifiers resolved against PubMed/PMC — 15 PMIDs, 12 PMCIDs and 19 DOIs — plus 61 identifier SITES in the text. EVERY ONE RESOLVES TO THE PAPER THE PROSE NAMES, and in every reference entry the PMID, PMCID and DOI printed together belong to the same paper (checked entry by entry for [1]–[15]; [2],[4],[5],[6],[7],[11],[12] each carry a PMID+PMCID+DOI triple and all seven agree). The erratum in [3] is real and correct: PMID 31579002 is 'Correction to Lancet Oncol 2019; 20: 1252-62', Lancet Oncol 2019;20(10):e559. The two congress abstracts [13] and [14] correctly share one container DOI — PMC9379246 / doi 10.1007/s00428-022-03379-4 is the 34th European Congress of Pathology abstract supplement, Virchows Arch 481(Suppl 1):1-364 — and OFP-04-002 and OFP-04-003 are both in it with the titles and case counts the manuscript states. EVERY PUBLICATION-TYPE CHARACTERISATION MATCHES THE RECORD: [2] is typed 'Case Reports' and is called a two-case index report; [4] and [5] are typed 'Review' and are called reviews; [3] is typed 'Clinical Trial, Phase II' and is called a phase 2 trial; Appendix A11's three re-characterisations are exact — PMC12398172 is Masunaga 2025, a 171-patient Japanese National Bone and Soft Tissue Tumor Registry cohort in J Orthop Surg Res (doi 10.1186/s13018-025-06245-6), PMC9131214 is a single-patient intracranial EMC case report in World J Clin Cases (doi 10.12998/wjcc.v10.i13.4301), and PMC12376927 is 'Diagnosis and Management of Large Extraosseous Myxoid Chondrosarcoma of the Buttocks: A Case Report', a 67-year-old man with a 40 cm buttock tumour, Am J Case Rep (doi 10.12659/AJCR.947135) — the characterisation the appendix says it obtained by web search is confirmed at source. A9's correction is also confirmed in both directions: PMID 36948401 is Huang SC et al., a Taiwanese cohort, and PMID 37057757 / doi 10.1002/gcc.23144 is a genuinely different Warmke LM et al. TAF15::NR4A3 paper, Genes Chromosomes Cancer 2023;62(10):581–588. 16 OF 18 VERBATIM QUOTATIONS ARE PRESENT WORD-FOR-WORD IN THE SOURCE NAMED (the two exceptions are unreachable, not wrong, and the manuscript discloses both). ONE bibliographic locator is wrong — reference [10]'s volume and pages (CI-P2-1) — and one quotation pair carries a second reference that does not contain it (CI-P2-2). No fabricated identifier was found; no identifier resolves to a different paper.
what_you_could_not_break: THE STARRED CHECK — the general TAF15 prevalence share and the figure the pooled estimate is compared against. Appendix A30's two quotations are verbatim and attributed to the right reference numbers. Reference [4] (Stacchiotti 2020, PMC7563993, doi 10.3390/cancers12092703) reads, in 'Pathological and Molecular Characteristics': 'less frequently (about 20% of cases) to the transactivation domain of TAF15 (aliases …), located on 17q12' — exactly as A30 quotes it, and it IS a disease review as A30 calls it. Reference [12] (Bangerter, PMC9813045, doi 10.1007/s13577-022-00818-x) reads, in its INTRODUCTION as A30 specifies: 'less frequently (approximately 20%) to TAF15 (TATA-Box Binding Protein Associated Factor 15)' — verbatim, and it IS a model-derivation paper. I searched the third review in the citation set, Remiszewski 2025 (PMC12504171, doi 10.1007/s00432-025-06316-5), for any general TAF15 share and found none, so A30's 'the two sources in this document's own reference list that state a general TAF15 share' is a correct count of the reference list. 20 % does fall inside 12.9–25.0. The retraction of the ≈27 % framing is right, and A3's residual reading is right too: 7/26 = 26.9 % is Agaram 2014's share on its all-tested denominator and 7/24 = 29.2 % on its partner-assigned one.

EVERY PREVALENCE INTEGER THE POOL RESTS ON, AT PRIMARY SOURCE. Agaram 2014 (PMC4015728): EWSR1 16 (62%), TAF15 7 (27%), TCF12 1 (4%), two NR4A3-only — 24 assigned, residue 2. Huang 2023 (PMID 36948401 abstract): '46 (79%), 9 (16%), and 2 (3%)' plus '1 (2%) NR4A3-rearranged EMC without identifiable partners' — 57 assigned, residue 1. Paioli 2021 (PMID 32572850 abstract): '50 (80%) NR4A3-EWS, 10 (16%) NR4A3-TAF15, 1 (2%) NR4A3-TCF12, and 1 (2%) NR4A3-TFG' of 67 — 62 assigned, residue 5. Lenz 11 assigned with residue 1 is consistent with 'molecular typing successful in 12 of 17'. 24+57+11+62 = 154 and 7+9+2+10 = 28, so 28/154 = 18.2 % is exactly reproduced from the sources, and the per-cohort range 15.8–29.2 is exactly Huang's 9/57 to Agaram's 7/24. §4.3's residue list '2, 1, 1 and 5' matches the four papers one for one.

THE TWO EXCLUDED CONGRESS ABSTRACTS' BRACKET, TO THE INTEGER. ECP 2022 OFP-04-002 (Valencia, 31 cases): 'The EWSR1-NR4A3 rearrangement was found in 19 cases and 7 patients presented the TAF-15-NR4A3 fusion' — 7 of 26 partner-assigned, exactly as §3.5 states, with a 5-case residue and no third partner class, exactly as §3.2's exclusion reason states. ECP 2022 OFP-04-003 (Czech, 11 cases): EWSR1 7/11, one TAF15 and one rarer fusion, one NR4A3-positive/EWSR1-negative — 1 of 9 partner-assigned, exactly as §3.5 states.

EVERY OUTCOME INTEGER ATTRIBUTED TO AGARAM 2014, AT PRIMARY SOURCE (PMC4015728, doi 10.1016/j.humpath.2014.01.007). EWSR1 arm n=16, mean follow-up 43.3 months, LR 1 (6%), DR 6 (37%), 1 DOD. TAF15 arm n=7, mean follow-up 21.7 months, 'Two (28%) patients each developed LR and DR', 'Three (43%) of the 7 … DOD'. Every one of §3.3's Agaram cells, §4.7's two-fold follow-up asymmetry and §3.2's '23 partner-assigned with follow-up' is reproduced. A4's correction is also exactly right: the 80 % is over the paper's ten-case variant group, and that group is 7 TAF15 + 1 TCF12 + 2 partner-unassigned as A4 says. And Agaram's own Discussion supports §3.3's metastasis null in the author's words: 'the rates of distant recurrences appear to be quite similar regardless of the fusion type.'

THE ATTRIBUTION CORRECTION IN §3.8, WHICH IS THE PAPER'S SHARPEST CITATION CLAIM AND IS CORRECT. 'Even in EMCS the fusion-protein is unlikely to be related to sunitinib sensitivity' is present VERBATIM in the Discussion of the 2012 two-case report (PMID 23058004, PMC3534218, doi 10.1186/2045-3329-2-22), and is NOT in the 2014 series' abstract, which instead says 'Genotype/phenotype analyses support a correlation between response and EWSR1-NR4A3 fusion' — also verbatim as quoted. §3.8's reading of the hedge as a 2012 PRIOR reasoned by analogy to alveolar soft part sarcoma is the source's own move: 'As shown in ASPS, another STS bearing a translocation, the antitumor activity of sunitinib is unlikely to be directly linked to the fusion-protein.' Both 2012 patients are EWSR1-translocated, as §3.2 states.

§3.1'S CLAIM THAT REVIEWS STATE THE NON-RESPONSE FLATLY. I went looking to break it and the record supports it twice: Jacobs & Lapeire 2021 (PMC7999686) writes 'indicating that TAF15-NR4A3 translocated EMCS is a more aggressive subgroup with insensitivity to antiangiogenic treatment', and Remiszewski 2025 (PMC12504171) writes 'Molecular analysis showed better outcomes in patients with the EWSR1 fusion, while TAF15 cases showed a poor response' with no denominator anywhere near it.

BRENCA 2019 AND BANGERTER, QUOTATION BY QUOTATION. Brenca (PMC6766969, doi 10.1002/path.5284): 7 EWSR1 and 5 TAF15 confirmed in Table 1; 'the ability of NR4A3 to recognize the SEMA3C target region was retained by the EWSR1-NR4A3 chimera but was impaired by TAF15-NR4A3' verbatim, and from a ChAP-qPCR experiment as §3.6 says; the SEMA3C/SEMA3G/RELN sentence present in the same construction (PMC strips italicised gene symbols, so the three symbols are recoverable only from context). §4.10's non-independence claim is verified rather than asserted: Brenca's author list contains Stacchiotti S, Casali PG, Pilotti S, Dagrada GP and Gronchi A, all of whom are authors on references [1], [2] and [3]. Bangerter (PMC9813045): all three §3.7 quotations verbatim, and A5's correction is exact — the 40-drug screen ran on USZ20-EMC1 alone ('A medium throughput drug screen using 40 drugs was conducted with USZ20-EMC1 at passage 5'), while carfilzomib, doxorubicin and venetoclax went forward to a validation step in both models, which is where the partner-independence sentences sit.

SUEMITSU 2025 AND THE OVERLAP GROUND §3.2 GIVES FOR HOLDING IT OUT. PMID 40828003 / doi 10.1002/gcc.70076 is 'Secondary Genetic Alterations in Extraskeletal Myxoid Chondrosarcoma', Genes Chromosomes Cancer 2025;64(8):e70076; 'Eighteen EMC patients (20 samples)'; 'two cases involved TAF15 gene partner'; and the quoted sentence is verbatim: 'no statistically significant correlation was detected between OS and fusion subtypes'. The MSK/MSKCC overlap concern is stronger than the manuscript states — the author list is Suemitsu Y, Chang HY, Saoud C, Dermawan JK, Hameed M, Singer S, Tap WD, Antonescu CR, and Singer S and Antonescu CR are both authors of Agaram 2014.

§3.5'S ABSOLUTE AUTHOR-DISJOINTNESS CLAIM, AND ITS FOUR COUNTS. The complete author lists from PubMed are 5 (Agaram), 20 (Huang), 18 (Lenz) and 16 (Paioli), exactly as §3.5 states, and the intersection is empty on all six pairs on surname alone as well as on surname-plus-initials. A26's repair holds.

THE INSTRUMENT ITSELF, WHERE IT REACHES. `test_fusion_partner_prose_matches_its_artifact.py` binds against DERIVED values rather than literals, checks EVERY site via `re.findall` rather than membership, requires at least one match so a reworded sentence goes red rather than quiet, and its section-G identifier tests are genuinely mutation-shaped: `test_identifiers_printed_in_one_reference_entry_belong_to_one_paper` catches the within-entry swap using the entry as grouping and the artifact as ownership with no hand-typed list, and `test_a_reference_entry_that_prints_a_papers_title_prints_that_papers_identifiers` catches the whole-entry swap using the artifact's verbatim title, with an `anchored >= 12` floor so a title drifting out of reach is audible. `_trim_doi`'s balanced-parenthesis rule is correct and load-bearing for reference [3]'s DOI. `_fold` is correct and necessary for Sjögren and Klubíčková. The module names exactly one manuscript basename, so `claim_coverage.py`'s basename-crediting hazard — which the docstring records as having once credited 82 false sentences to a different paper — is closed here.
